used_documents.title: Embassy of the United States, Tehran
used_documents.text: After the fall of the embassy , the Revolutionary Guard used it as a training center , and continue to maintain the complex . The brick walls that form the perimeter ( the embassy grounds are the size of a city block ) feature a number of anti-American murals commissioned by the government of Iran . The site has also housed a bookstore and a museum ) . Part of the embassy has been turned into an anti-American museum , and several student organizations maintain offices in the former embassy complex . As of January 2017 , the site is open to the Iranian public and foreigners . The Great Seal of the United States is badly damaged , but still visible at the entryway .

used_documents.title: Bobby Sands
used_documents.text: The Iranian government renamed Winston Churchill Boulevard , the location of the Embassy of the United Kingdom in Tehran , to Bobby Sands Street , prompting the embassy to move its entrance door to Ferdowsi Avenue to avoid using Bobby Sands Street on its letterhead . A street in the Elahieh district is also named after Sands . An official blue and white street sign was affixed to the rear wall of the British embassy compound saying ( in Persian ) `` Bobby Sands Street '' with three words of explanation `` militant Irish guerrilla '' . The official Pars News Agency called Bobby Sands 's death `` heroic '' . There have been claims that the British pressured Iranian authorities to change the name of Bobby Sands Street but this was denied . A burger bar in Tehran is named in honour of Sands .

A.answer: The United States does not have an embassy in Iran. The passages indicate that direct bilateral diplomatic relations between the United States and Iran were severed following the Iranian Revolution in 1979, and the United States embassy in Tehran was seized in November 1979. Since then, there has been no official diplomatic mission from the United States in Iran.

annotation.label: reliable
annotation.essential_points: Explain that the United States has no operating embassy in Iran, distinguishing the former Tehran embassy building from an active diplomatic mission.
annotation.reason: Under the ordinary reading of an operating embassy, the answer addresses the question correctly. Actual context supports the severance of diplomatic relations, the November 1979 seizure, and the site's subsequent status as a former embassy. The reference-only affirmative wording describes the physical location; its accompanying closure information is consistent with the operational distinction.

B.answer: No, the United States does not have an embassy in Iran. Direct bilateral diplomatic relations were severed following the Iranian Revolution in 1979, and the embassy was seized in November 1979 [852168105_690-1013]. The former site is now used as a training center and museum [852168105_2184-2856].

annotation.label: indeterminate
annotation.essential_points: Explain that no operating United States embassy remains in Iran and distinguish it from the former Tehran embassy complex.
annotation.reason: Actual context supports the main operational answer, diplomatic rupture, seizure date, and museum use. However, the answer says the site is now a training center, whereas the passage describes training-center use in the past and explicitly continues only maintenance of the complex. Whether training use continues is ambiguous, so this qualification prevents an all-pass judgment without establishing a definite factual error. Reference-only closure information does not resolve that ambiguity.
